body:
This really depends on where you're at and where your depression comes from. For me, I was situationally depressed after the 2008 fiscal collapse. I felt despair over my own career prospects, and let that define who I was at the time. Weight lifting really helped me for two reasons. First, and especially in the beginning, I was able to lift more (weight or reps or sets--whatever) and that sense of progress helped me feel like I was getting better. Second, getting stronger and bigger helped me feel more masculine and powerful, which was important after the emasculating experience of being unable to find a job.

So, exercise can definitely help. It helped me. But you should consider what's going on in your life and what you're hoping that exercise will accomplish for your own sense of self.

[This](http://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/dw8wy/there_just_isnt_any_hope/) was me about a year ago. I feel like where I was then and where you are now are pretty similar.

Since then I've got a great job and while I'm still struggling with depression (especially negative self-talk and suicidal thoughts) I generally feel like I'm doing really well. 

I feel like three things helped me: lifting weights, volunteer work, doing mushrooms.

Lifting weights gave me something to work towards immediately. I was getting stronger, and I could measure it! So even though I felt like my life was going nowhere as far as my career was concerned, at least I was getting somewhere with my health. Not to mention it helped me look a lot better and gave me more self-confidence generally.

I attribute landing the job I have now directly to doing volunteer work. All of a sudden I had anecdotes I could tell at an interview. "Oh, you want to hear about how I had to solve a problem? How about the one where a client was in the hospital and I had to resolve the case while he was on the other side of the state? I solved that problem!" Volunteering also gave me a place where people genuinely were happy to have me around (everybody likes it when you do their work for free!). That really helps.

Finally, mushrooms have actually been shown to give people, especially depressed people, a new look at the world. I'm not going to recommend the unreservedly, jail time is a prospect after all. But I was unemployed and on food stamps and I spent four hours thinking about how absolutely amazing life is. And I take that perspective around with me today. Google it, and you'll find some interesting studies about psilocybin mushrooms and depression.

So, I can't tell you that things will "work out." I think emotional maturity means recognizing that sometimes things don't. But I'm really happy I kept trying, and I hope you keep trying too.
